lines: -- The OpenPGP API now implements RFC 9980 (Post-Quantum Cryptography in OpenPGP): the ML-DSA-65+Ed25519 and ML-DSA-87+Ed448 composite signature algorithms (IDs 30 and 31), the SLH-DSA-SHAKE-128s, -128f and -256s signature algorithms (32 to 34) and the ML-KEM-768+X25519 and ML-KEM-1024+X448 composite encryption algorithms (35 and 36), with the key material, PKESK and signature packet layouts, the SHA3-256 key combiner and AES-256 key wrap of the composite KEMs, and the version, digest-size and v3 PKESK symmetric algorithm rules the RFC imposes. PGPKeyPairGenerator, BcPGPKeyPairGeneratorProvider and JcaPGPKeyPairGeneratorProvider generate the keys (BcPGPCompositeKeyParameters and CompositePublicKey/CompositePrivateKey carry the two component keys in the lightweight and JCA operators), the Bc and Jce key converters, encryption method generators, data decryptor factories, content signer builders and content verifier builder providers operate with them, OpenPGPKeyGenerator gains the mlDsa65Ed25519MlKem768X25519Key, mlDsa87Ed448MlKem1024X448Key and slhDsaShake*MlKem*Key profiles, OpenPGPDefaultPolicy accepts the new algorithms, and the encryption negotiator applies the RFC 9980 sec. 7.1 implicit AES-256 preference of a certificate carrying a PQ(/T) key. The Appendix A test vectors of the RFC drive the tests.

+- The OpenPGP API now implements RFC 9980 (Post-Quantum Cryptography in OpenPGP): the ML-DSA-65+Ed25519 and ML-DSA-87+Ed448 composite signature algorithms (IDs 30 and 31), the SLH-DSA-SHAKE-128s, -128f and -256s signature algorithms (32 to 34) and the ML-KEM-768+X25519 and ML-KEM-1024+X448 composite encryption algorithms (35 and 36), with the key material, PKESK and signature packet layouts, the SHA3-256 key combiner and AES-256 key wrap of the composite KEMs, and the version, digest-size, v3 PKESK symmetric algorithm and no-SED rules the RFC imposes. PGPKeyPairGenerator, BcPGPKeyPairGeneratorProvider and JcaPGPKeyPairGeneratorProvider generate the keys (BcPGPCompositeKeyParameters and CompositePublicKey/CompositePrivateKey carry the two component keys in the lightweight and JCA operators), the Bc and Jce key converters, encryption method generators, data decryptor factories, content signer builders and content verifier builder providers operate with them, OpenPGPKeyGenerator gains the mlDsa65Ed25519MlKem768X25519Key, mlDsa87Ed448MlKem1024X448Key and slhDsaShake*MlKem*Key profiles, OpenPGPDefaultPolicy accepts the new algorithms, and the encryption negotiator applies the RFC 9980 sec. 7.1 implicit AES-256 preference of a certificate carrying a PQ(/T) key. The Appendix A test vectors of the RFC drive the tests.

- org.bouncycastle.cbor.c509.C509PrivateKeyPossessionStatement is the C509 form of the RFC 9883 privateKeyPossessionStatement attribute, converting to and from the ASN.1 org.bouncycastle.asn1.x509.PrivateKeyPossessionStatement, and C509CertificationRequestBuilder.setPrivateKeyPossessionStatement() carries one in a natively signed request.

- HQC now implements the HQC team's specification of 2026-10-12, which supersedes the 2025-08-22 version the 1.86 release followed, and tracks the reference implementation that goes with it. The decapsulation key is now the 32-byte seedKEM alone, the compressed format the earlier specification offered as an alternative and the format NIST has said it intends to make the only one in FIPS 207, so an HQC private key encodes as 32 bytes for every parameter set where it was 2321, 4602 or 7333; HQCPrivateKeyParameters re-derives the expanded key the first time it is used and keeps it, the caching the specification allows, and gains getPublicKeyParameters(). The parameters change with the team's improved decoding failure rate analysis: the weight of the secret vectors rises by one for all three sets (67, 101 and 132) and the weight of the encryption randomness by one for hqc-128 and hqc-256 (76 and 150), leaving the public key and ciphertext sizes as they were. The Reed-Solomon code now works over GF(2^8) defined by X^8 + X^4 + X^3 + X + 1 rather than X^8 + X^4 + X^3 + X^2 + 1, with the generator polynomials and power tables regenerated for it, and the RM(1,7) generator matrix is the one the specification now writes out, which reverses the bit order within each codeword byte. The XOF no longer appends a domain byte to its seed, the expansion of seedKEM absorbs the parameter set's k after it as the reference implementation does, and the fixed-weight sampler used for the secret key draws its 3-byte candidates one at a time and little-endian. Keys, ciphertexts and shared secrets from earlier releases are incompatible with this one. The known-answer tests are the reference implementation's for this version, which seed the NIST AES-256 CTR-DRBG as the other NIST candidates' tests do.

- The Merkle Tree Certificate support in org.bouncycastle.cert.plants and org.bouncycastle.asn1.plants now tracks draft-ietf-plants-merkle-tree-certs-07, which allocates the production object identifiers and changes several of draft-05's wire formats incompatibly. MTCObjectIdentifiers carries the allocated values, id-alg-mtcProof 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.6.67, id-rdna-trustAnchorID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.25.3 and id-pe-mtcCertificationAuthority-SHA256 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.1.38, in place of the interim Cloudflare PEN arcs, with no aliases; the issuer and subject names carry the CA ID as a RELATIVE-OID rather than a UTF8String (the UTF8String form is still read); the signatures field of MTCProof has a three-byte length prefix; the MTCCertificationAuthority extension is SEQUENCE { sigAlg, minSerial, maxSerial }, the log hash being identified by the extension type, which MTCCertificationAuthorityCertificate.logHashAlgorithm() reports, with serial bounds of 2^48..2^64-1; empty subtrees [x, x) are valid, the Merkle Tree Hash of an empty range is HASH("") with an empty consistency proof, and the Section 4.5.1 covering procedure always returns two subtrees; and the published landmark document carries an expiry time per landmark in place of the max_active_landmarks count, with LandmarkSequence gaining isActive(), landmarkSubtrees(), landmarkFor() and landmarkSubtreeFor() for the Section 6.4.4 construction. The Appendix C.1 accumulated test vectors are updated to draft-07's values, GREASE cosignatures under an unrecognised cosigner ID are ignored as Section 7.2 requires, and the trust anchor IDs TrustAnchorIDs builds are bounded at 32 bytes per draft-ietf-tls-trust-anchor-ids-06. The classes follow the draft's renamed structures: MerkleTreeCertEntry, MerkleTreeCertEntryExtension and MerkleTreeCertEntryType are now MTCLogEntry, MTCLogEntryExtension and MTCLogEntryType, MTCSignature is MTCCosignature and MTCCosignedMessage is MTCCosignedSubtree, with the old names kept as deprecated subclasses of the new ones; MTCProof.getSignatures() and MTCCosigner.cosignSubtree() now return the new types. As the package has only tracked a draft, the following are breaking API changes rather than deprecations: the MTCCertificationAuthority constructors taking a log hash AlgorithmIdentifier and its getLogHash() method are removed, the extension now being built from a signature algorithm and the two serial bounds; the LandmarkSequence constructor takes a third array of landmark expiry times and the two-array constructor and the previous parse()/format() document layout are gone; MTCObjectIdentifiers.id_pe_mtcCertificationAuthority and the Cloudflare placeholder constants are removed, with no alias to the new values; implementations of the MTCCosigner interface must return MTCCosignature from cosignSubtree(); TrustAnchorIDs.MAX_ID_LENGTH changes from 255 to 32, a compile-time constant that stays inlined at 255 in code built against 1.86 until it is recompiled, and X509Extension.id_rdna_trustAnchorID changes from the bare 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.25 arc to 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.25.3; and MerkleTreePrimitives and ListMerkleTreeNodeSource now accept an empty range where 1.86 threw or returned false, so callers relying on that rejection need their own check.
